The theory of evolution is a school of thought based on theoretical models consistent with empirical observations. You could choose to invest mental energy into different schools of thought. The utility of some of those alternative schools of thought might have poor predictive power for the resultant attributes of the nth generation of fruitflies with a specific environmental stressor, but they might genuinely and accurately speak to a different phenomenon altogether (or they might not). If we put Darwin's own model of evolution under scrutiny, he too missed large pieces of the puzzle that are now incorperated into the modern conventional models (e.g. epigenetics, etc). Using a "one mutation at a time at X rate" probably isn't going to give you a strong basis to criticize conventional models, largely because that is not how expressed mutations work.
